design:
- D1 — The loop only awaits. Git, filesystem scans and process spawns that serve a request, a turn start, an approval or a background job run off the event loop. Their results are applied to the database on the loop. Why: a 4s freeze stops every agent and every screen, not only the caller.
- D2 — Blocking work does not compete with streaming runs for threads. Git and file work waiting for a thread are never queued behind the blocking reads of live runs. Why: each live Claude run holds a pooled thread for its whole turn, and a weak VDI has fewer.
- D3 — Streamed output lines are recorded in batches. A burst of lines is persisted together rather than with one session and commit per line. A line is still on screen as soon as the Hub receives it, and still persisted before the run is reported finished. Why: about 5ms per line on every runner, plus the per-line trace span rewrite.
- D4 — Unchanged facts are not recomputed per request.
  - Which runner binaries exist is cached for the process and re-checked when runners change.
  - Whether a root is a git repository is cached per root.
  - A parsed spec document is reused until its file changes.
- D5 — Outcomes are unchanged. Every turn, approval, merge, evidence footprint, review staffing and mender brief produces the same records as before. Only where the work runs changes.
- Runner-agnostic (roadmap): the drive starts real turns on Claude and Copilot, and replays a recorded Codex stream until a Codex account exists.
- Hazard: turn start and approval are the paths that create and release worktrees and merge to the main branch. A race introduced here corrupts a checkout or a merge. Tier 2 by CLAUDE.md (cross-cutting contract); the acceptance drive is written and failing before the build.

problem:
The Hub serves every request and background job on one event loop. Work that blocks that loop stops everything: every dashboard read, every agent's tool call and every stream. The figures come from the operator's traces (7,149 git spans, 2026-10-21 to 10-25), a call-graph scan and a loop-lag sampler on a copy of the database (`C:\Users\huida\aw-perf\C-loop-blockers.md`).

Blocking git and file work found on the loop:

| Path | Where | Fires | Freeze per occurrence | Total over 90 h |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Turn start: workspace resolution and creation, plus about 4 rev-parse checks | `hub/hub/api/v1/agent_trigger.py:1290,1497,1522-1524,1533,1551,1570` | Every turn | 1.02s average, p95 4.2s, max 20.8s | 238s |
| Approval releases the task checkout | `hub/hub/task_transition_service.py:1032` | Every approval | 4.2s average, p95 10.3s | 79s |
| Approval merges the work | `task_transition_service.py:1241,1283,1299` | Every approval | 686ms average, max 2.1s | 23s |
| Recording evidence (7 git calls) | `hub/hub/requirement_evidence.py:215,436,720` | Each record | 332ms | 58s |
| Re-stamping footprints at run end | `agent_trigger.py:2664`, `requirement_evidence.py:1637-1673` | Each run end | 345ms | — |
| Review staffing | `hub/hub/review_turn.py:582,619-638` | Each review | 665ms, max 2.9s | 21s |
| Mender brief runs `git status` | `hub/hub/stalls.py:600` | Each mender wake | up to 2.9s | — |
| Drift detection | `hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py:1965-1976` | Each run | 426ms | — |
| Spec list re-reads and re-parses every document file | `hub/hub/spec_documents.py:703`, called from `api/v1/spec.py:129` | Every `GET /project/specs` | 454ms (504 path resolutions, 850 stats, 162 parses) | — |
| `shutil.which` and `is_git_repo` | launchability, queue-status, worktree and workspace routes | Per request | 3-30ms | — |

Per-line cost and thread capacity:
- Each streamed output line costs about 5ms of loop time on every runner. That covers its own session and commit (`agent_trigger.py:3383`, `:2824`, `hub/hub/output_recording.py:135`) and a whole reload and rewrite of the run's chat trace span (`hub/hub/traces.py:266-307`).
- Each live Claude run holds a thread of the default executor in a blocking read (`agent_trigger.py:3509`). That is the same pool `asyncio.to_thread` uses: 24 threads on this machine, and fewer on a smaller VDI. Moving git onto it naively would make git wait behind streaming runs.

requirements.rationale: Measured today: 1.02s average, up to 20.8s per turn start, during which every request waits.
requirements.statement: While a turn starts on any runner, including creating its task checkout, the Hub's event loop never stalls for more than 100ms at a time.

requirements.rationale: Measured today: releasing a checkout averages 4.2s and a merge can take up to 2.1s, both on the loop.
requirements.statement: While a task is approved, including releasing its checkout and merging its work, the Hub's event loop never stalls for more than 100ms at a time.

requirements.rationale: Each path runs git on the loop today: 332ms, 345ms, 665ms (max 2.9s), up to 2.9s and 426ms respectively.
requirements.statement: Recording evidence, re-stamping footprints when a run ends, staffing a review, briefing the mender and detecting drift each leave no event-loop stall longer than 100ms.

requirements.rationale: Measured today: about 5ms per line, from a session and commit per line plus a full rewrite of the run's chat span.
requirements.statement: While a run streams 90 output lines a minute on any runner, the Hub spends on average no more than 1.5ms of event-loop time per line recording it.

requirements.rationale: Batching must not delay what the operator sees, and must not lose lines when a run ends or the Hub stops.
requirements.statement: A streamed output line reaches open dashboards within 250ms of the Hub receiving it. Every line a run produced is persisted before the run is reported finished.

requirements.rationale: Each live Claude run holds a thread in a blocking read, so blocking work moved off the loop must not queue behind them, least of all on a smaller VDI.
requirements.statement: With eight runs streaming at once, git or file work the Hub sends off the event loop starts within 100ms of being requested.

requirements.rationale: Measured today: 454ms and 173ms, re-reading and re-parsing every document file on the loop for each request.
requirements.statement: GET /project/specs and GET /project/documents answer in under 100ms on this repository when no spec file changed since the previous request, without stalling the event loop for more than 100ms.

requirements.rationale: This slice moves where work runs, not what it does. A worktree or merge that differs is a correctness defect, not a speed-up.
requirements.statement: For the same inputs, turn starts, approvals, merges, evidence footprints, review staffing and mender briefs produce the same database records and git state as before this change.

in_scope: Git, filesystem and process work reached from async code on the turn-start, approval, merge, evidence, run-end, review-staffing, mender-brief, drift and spec-listing paths
How streamed output lines are persisted, on every runner
Thread capacity for blocking work alongside streaming runs
Per-request caching of runner binary lookups, git-repository checks and parsed spec documents
non_goals: Making git itself faster (worktree add still takes about 4s; it just stops freezing the Hub)
The routes that already run their git in a thread (worktrees/conflicts, the evidence diff): they are slow but do not block
Changing what any turn, approval, merge or evidence record contains

summary: Starting a turn, approving a task, recording evidence, staffing a review, briefing the mender and streaming output lines stop freezing every other request while git, the filesystem or the database works. This must hold on every runner path (Claude, Copilot, Codex). On the operator's Hub these freezes total about 400s over 90 hours, up to 20.8s each.
